(Ireland) An evening funeral ritual in which the coffin holding the deceased is brought, usually from a funeral home, to the church where the funeral mass will be celebrated the following day. Prayers are said before and after the journey, after which mourners are typically received at the home of the deceased.
The act of refusing.
The Kingdom of the Netherlands. A country in Western Europe, consisting of four constituent countries: the Netherlands per se, Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten.
A traditional region of the Netherlands formed by two modern provinces, North Holland and South Holland.
Voltage.
The difference in electrostatic potential between two points in space, especially between live and neutral conductors or the earth.
A suspenseful, sensational genre of story, book, play, film.
The unpleasant emotion of anxiety or apprehension in an uncertain situation.

Wearing nothing on the feet.

A light, silvery metal extracted from bauxite, and a chemical element (symbol Al) with an atomic number of 13.
Any great, strong, powerful emotion, especially romantic love or extreme hate.
A habit or practice that damages, jeopardizes or shortens one's life but when ceased causes trauma.

A high area; land that is higher than surrounding areas.

Any of various species of insects, many of them nocturnal, in the family Myrmeleontidae. The adults superficially resemble the unrelated damselflies. The larvae bury themselves in sand below a cone-shaped pit in which they trap insects such as ants.
An expression of praise, congratulation, or respect.
An instance of shaving.
The act of cutting of the hair, often done professionally by a barber, hair stylist, or beautician.
The ordinal form of the number sixty-eight, describing a person or thing in position number 68 of a sequence.

Overly proud of oneself, especially concerning appearance; having a high opinion of one's own accomplishments with slight reason.
Full of pride.

Tending to stick; able to adhere via the drying of a viscous substance.
Having cohesion.
Clinging to an object or surface; adhesive.
Soft, sticky and viscous.
Glue-like, sticky, viscid.

Confidence, pride.
Self-confidence; poise; composure.

Inclined to peace.
Willing to comply; submissive; willing to do what someone wants.
Affording, or disposed to afford, accommodation; obliging; helpful.
Disposed or prone to indulge, humor, gratify, or yield to one's own or another's desires, etc., or to be compliant, lenient, or forbearing.
Ready to accept instruction or direction; obedient; subservient.
Any mammal of the many rodent families (especially Muridae) that have a small body and a long tail.

The capital city of Basel-Stadt canton, Switzerland.
Having no brain.

Angled at a slant.

An outburst, especially of laughter.

A rich purple synthetic dye, which faded easily, briefly popular c. 1859‒1873 and now called mauveine.
An opportunity or possibility.
something that happens to someone by chance
Good fortune.
Being overly concerned with formal rules and trivial points of learning, like a pedant.
(mildly, vulgar) An insolent person, especially one who makes snide remarks.
A person who makes an excessive or tedious show of their knowledge, especially regarding rules of vocabulary and grammar.
One who feigns knowledge or cleverness; one who is wisecracking; an insolent upstart.
documentary evidence of someone's right to credit or authority
A chamber in or attachable to a firearm enabling multiple rounds of ammunition to be fed into the firearm.
(chemistry) Any salt or ester of phosphoric acid.
An ancient city and archaeological site in Jordan.
A sullen, gloomy or angry mental state; a bad mood.
State of mind; mood.

A usually translucent and somewhat elastic, dense, nonvascular connective tissue found in various forms in the larynx and respiratory tract, in structures such as the external ear, and in the articulating surfaces of joints. It composes most of the skeleton of vertebrate embryos, being replaced by bone during ossification in the higher vertebrates.
Cartilage; now especially: cartilage present, as a tough substance, in meat.
An unincorporated community in Phillips County, Kansas, located in the north of the state off U.S. Route 36 7.6 mi west-northwest of Phillipsburg and 6.6 mi east-southeast of Prairie View.
Suggestive of an earlier event or times.
A port city in northern Greece.
The young shoots of Asparagus officinalis eaten as a vegetable.
A silent and reserved nature.
Of or pertaining to the female sex; biologically female, not male.
(Ancient Greece) A celebrated Greek statesman and orator (389–314 B.C.E.; full name Αἰσχίνης Ἀτρομήτου Κοθωκίδης, Aeschines Atrometi f. Cothocides), one the Canon of Ten Attic Orators.
A department of Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France. Capital: Moulins (INSEE code 03).
The state of being clueless.
The quality of being imbecile; weakness; feebleness, especially of mind.
The use of the lips, facial muscles, tongue, and teeth when playing a wind instrument.
Any plant of the genus Anemone, of the Ranunculaceae (or buttercup) family, such as the windflower.
tendency to attract
A plant of the obsolete genus Azalea.
A pen or enclosure for sheep or other domestic animals.

An enclosed piece of land, usually small and arable and used for small-scale food production, and often with a dwelling next to it; in particular, such a piece of land rented to a farmer (a crofter), especially in Scotland, together with a right to use separate pastureland shared by other crofters.
(also, figuratively) A small enclosure or field of grassland, especially one used to exercise or graze horses or other animals.

To express displeasure or indignation at.

A fine-grained igneous rock composed mostly of pyroxene and feldspar.

Being in the passive voice.
The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, ε or Ε, preceded by delta (Δ, δ) and followed by zeta (Ζ, ζ).

One of two or more different words in a language derived from the same etymological root but having different phonological forms (e.g., toucher and toquer in French or shade and shadow in English). See also Appendix:Glossary#doublet.

A state of nature; conformity to nature.

The currency of Ukraine, symbol ₴, divided into 100 kopiykas.
A division of a political unit.
A framework of such posts, used to secure or confine cattle.

Any of several flightless sea birds, of the family Spheniscidae within the order Sphenisciformes, found in the Southern Hemisphere, marked by their usual upright stance, walking on short legs, and (generally) their stark black and white plumage.
Potassium or sodium hydroxide (caustic soda).
A cover of minute ice crystals on objects that are exposed to the air. Frost is formed by the same process as dew, except that the temperature of the frosted object is below freezing.
A shiny, decorative adornment, sometimes sprinkled on glue to make simple artwork.
Moisture in the air that settles on plants, etc in the morning or evening, resulting in drops.

(Greek god) A Titaness and the personification of thought, intellect and memory. She is the daughter of Gaia and Uranus, and the mother of the Muses by Zeus.
Suitable or fit; proper; felicitous.
An old woman, especially a wrinkly one.
A separate streamlined enclosure mounted on an aircraft to house, originally, an engine, and now also cargo or crew.
The homeostatic regulation of osmotic pressure in the body in order to maintain a certain water content (concentration of electrolytes, pH, etc).
A large triangular bone at the base of the spine, located between the two ilia (wings of the pelvis) and formed from vertebrae that fuse in adulthood.
